questions.q: What are the four stages of the threat hunting loop, in order?
options: Form a hypothesis, gather data, analyze, document findings — then refine and repeat
Detect, contain, eradicate, recover
Scan, patch, monitor, report
Collect logs, delete logs, re-collect logs, archive logs
questions.explain: The loop is: form a hypothesis, gather data, analyze, document findings, and then refine and repeat regardless of outcome.

questions.q: In the lesson's worked example, what does "gather data" mean for the rundll32.exe LOLBin hypothesis?
options: Pulling every rundll32.exe process-creation event across the environment, with full command-line arguments, over a defined window
Deleting all existing antivirus logs before starting the hunt
Interviewing end users about whether they noticed anything unusual
Immediately isolating every workstation in the environment
questions.explain: Gathering data means pulling the specific process-creation logs that could confirm or rule out the exact hypothesis formed in Lesson 25.

questions.q: Why is a hunt that finds no matching activity still considered a successful, worthwhile hunt?
options: It produces a real, documented confirmation that the specific technique isn't present, which is useful information on its own
It isn't successful — any hunt that finds nothing should be deleted from the record
It means the hypothesis was poorly formed and should never be reused
It automatically proves the entire environment is fully secure
questions.explain: A documented negative finding is genuinely useful — it's different from never having looked, and it still belongs in the hunting record.

questions.q: What does "analyze" involve in this lesson's version of the loop?
options: Baselining normal activity in the specific environment, then filtering gathered data for the pattern the hypothesis predicted
Immediately writing a scheduled analytics rule without reviewing any data
Discarding the hypothesis and starting over with a completely different one
Notifying executive leadership before any data has been reviewed
questions.explain: Analysis means comparing what came back against a baseline of normal behavior to spot the pattern the hypothesis was testing for.

questions.q: Why is threat hunting described as a loop rather than a one-time task?
options: Whether a hunt finds something or not, the team refines and goes back to stage one with a sharper or new hypothesis
Because regulations require every hunt to be repeated exactly three times
Because a hunting query, once written, automatically becomes a permanent detection
Because every hunt must end with a declared incident
questions.explain: The refine-and-repeat stage is what makes this an ongoing practice — a confirmed hit or a clean result both lead back into the loop.
